integration_issues.flow: Head Out wizard Step 3 → Start journey → active session screen
integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL, UNFIXED: Tapping 'Start journey' (headout-start-journey) throws a runtime error 'google api is already presented' within ~500ms, which crashes the circle.tsx tree. RootErrorBoundary catches it and the app effectively does a full reset — landing back on an UNAUTHENTICATED-looking /women/head-out/destination Step-1 screen ('Sign in to see and save your places') instead of the active /women/head-out session with countdown. The session write to AsyncStorage DOES happen before the crash, but the user never gets to see it — the happy path never completes visibly. RCA: both src/women/DestinationMapPicker.web.tsx and src/women/ActiveJourneyMap.web.tsx independently use the `<LoadScript>` component from @react-google-maps/api (not the shared `useJsApiLoader` hook / a single app-level loader). @react-google-maps/api explicitly does not support mounting more than one LoadScript instance in the same page lifecycle — when destination.tsx's map is still tearing down while head-out.tsx's ActiveJourneyMap mounts its own LoadScript, the second instance throws this exact error. This is a NEW bug distinct from the Leaflet-import fix described in the handoff — it's in the Google Maps branch of these same two files, not the Leaflet fallback branch.

react_native_issues.issue: FIXED during this session: radius.tsx imported RADIUS_PRESETS, isPreset, CustomRadiusModal as named exports from DestinationPicker.tsx, but none of the three were exported (module-private consts/functions). This is NOT one of the 44 dismissed TS-strictness errors — `npx tsc --noEmit` flags it distinctly as TS2459 ('declares X locally, but it is not exported'), and at runtime it crashed Step 2 of the wizard with a React red-screen ('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading map)') on every navigation from destination.tsx to radius.tsx. Fixed by adding `export` to all three declarations in DestinationPicker.tsx. Verified: tsc now clean for radius.tsx, and Step 1 -> Step 2 -> Step 3 navigation works with destination/radius data correctly carried across (confirmed TEST_Connaught Place shown on Step 2, 300m selection reflected on Step 3's handleStartJourney payload).

critical_code_review_comments: app/women/head-out.tsx is 1316 lines — well over the 700-line guideline; should be split (e.g. extract the GPS/route-deviation/escalation logic, the expired/arrived/deviated card renderers, and the change-destination modal into separate files).

tsc --noEmit module-resolution/export errors (TS2459 in this case) are a cheap, fast, genuinely non-type-strictness class of bug the main agent's stated verification method (counting only 'cannot find module' errors) would have missed — worth re-running `tsc --noEmit | grep -v <known-44-list>` rather than eyeballing, since this round found exactly one more real bug that slipped through that way.

rca_of_issue: Two distinct root causes found: (1) app/women/head-out/radius.tsx imported RADIUS_PRESETS/isPreset/CustomRadiusModal from DestinationPicker.tsx as named exports, but DestinationPicker.tsx never exported them (module-private). Confirmed via `npx tsc --noEmit` (TS2459) and reproduced live (red-screen 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading map)' on Step 2 every time). Fixed by adding `export`. (2) app/women/head-out/circle.tsx's 'Start journey' button calls router.replace('/women/head-out'), which mounts head-out.tsx's ActiveJourneyMap.web.tsx; this mounts a SECOND `<LoadScript>` from @react-google-maps/api while destination.tsx's own DestinationMapPicker.web.tsx `<LoadScript>` instance may still be tearing down from the previous screen — @react-google-maps/api throws 'google api is already presented' when this happens, since it's only designed for one LoadScript instance per page lifecycle. This crash is caught by RootErrorBoundary, which resets app state (web preview doesn't persist auth across this kind of reset the same way a manual browser reload doesn't either — confirmed this specific logout behavior is pre-existing/expected for this web preview in general, not a new regression, by reproducing it with a plain manual page reload unrelated to Head Out).
